1420631a2	bzip2/libbzip2: internal error number %d.
1420631cc	This is a bug in bzip2/libbzip2, %s.
1420631f1	Please report it to me at: jseward@bzip.org.  If this happened
142063230	when you were using some program which uses libbzip2 as a
14206326a	component, you should also report this bug to the author(s)
1420632a6	of that program.  Please make an effort to report this bug;
1420632e2	timely and accurate bug reports eventually lead to higher
14206331c	quality software.  Thanks.  Julian Seward, 10 December 2007.
142063361	*** A special note about internal error number 1007 ***
14206339a	Experience suggests that a common cause of i.e. 1007
1420633cf	is unreliable memory or other hardware.  The 1007 assertion
14206340b	just happens to cross-check the results of huge numbers of
142063446	memory reads/writes, and so acts (unintendedly) as a stress
142063482	test of your memory system.
14206349f	I suggest the following: try compressing the file again,
1420634d8	possibly monitoring progress in detail with the -vv flag.
142063513	* If the error cannot be reproduced, and/or happens at different
142063554	  points in compression, you may have a flaky memory system.
142063591	  Try a memory-test program.  I have used Memtest86
1420635c5	  (www.memtest86.com).  At the time of writing it is free (GPLd).
142063607	  Memtest86 tests memory much more thorougly than your BIOSs
142063644	  power-on test, and may find failures that the BIOS doesn't.
142063683	* If the error can be repeatably reproduced, this is a bug in
1420636c1	  bzip2, and I would very much like to hear about it.  Please
1420636ff	  let me know, and, ideally, save a copy of the file causing the
142063740	  problem -- without which I will be unable to investigate it.
